name: chevron-holds-through-a-fold-under-a-still-pointer
description: A fold or unfold under a still pointer must keep the chevron up the whole time, on a folder head and on the workspace name row. The echoed push rebuilds the rail with replaceChildren, and a rebuilt head has no :hover until Chromium's next hover update - sidebar.js carryHover marks it .hoverhold so the glyph (.fic-g / .wsic-i) never paints. The probe is a rAF sampler armed in the page before the click: it records the max computed opacity of the held head's glyph across ~3s. Pre-fix the glyph jumps to 1 and fades over .15s, so the sampler reads ~1; post-fix it stays 0. The apply-count delta makes the pass non-vacuous: a run where no rebuild happened cannot report 'held'. Real cgevent input, not synthetic JS events, because the whole bug lives in Chromium's hover bookkeeping.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
park in page content so nothing in the sidebar starts hovered

actions.expression: (() => { const r = (el) => { if (!el) return null; const b = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return [Math.round(b.x), Math.round(b.y), Math.round(b.width), Math.round(b.height)]; }; return JSON.stringify({ws: r(document.querySelector('.wsname')), news: r(document.querySelector('.row.frow'))}); })()
actions.note: page-space rects of the two heads, to correct the cgevent coordinates below when they miss
the settled sidebar, for measuring the screen positions the rects map onto
over the News folder head. Page rect from the rects eval: y 207 h 36, and the workspace head (page mid 108) hovers at screen 143, so content maps to screen at +35
the pointer really sits on the folder head before anything is armed

actions.expression: (() => { const head = document.querySelector('.frow:hover'); if (!head) return 'NOHOVER'; const id = head.dataset.folderId; const st = {id, max: 0, ticks: 0, applies0: window.__atriumApplyCount || 0, bad: []}; window.__chevhold = st; const tick = () => { const h = document.querySelector(`.frow[data-folder-id="${CSS.escape(id)}"]`); const g = h && h.querySelector('.fic-g, .wsic-i'); if (!h) { if (st.bad.length < 12) st.bad.push({t: st.ticks, gone: 1}); } else if (g) { const o = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(g).opacity); if (o > 0.01 && st.bad.length < 12) st.bad.push({t: st.ticks, o: +o.toFixed(2), hov: h.matches(':hover') ? 1 : 0, hold: h.classList.contains('hoverhold') ? 1 : 0, ap: (window.__atriumApplyCount || 0) - st.applies0}); if (o > st.max) st.max = o; } st.ticks++; if (st.ticks < 200) requestAnimationFrame(tick); }; requestAnimationFrame(tick); return 'ARMED'; })()

actions.note: the echoed push is parked ~320ms (FOLD_SETTLE_MS) before the rebuild the sampler is watching for

actions.expression: (() => { const st = window.__chevhold; if (!st) return 'NOSTATE'; const applies = (window.__atriumApplyCount || 0) - st.applies0; const verdict = st.max <= 0.01 ? 'held' : 'flashed'; const base = verdict + ' applies=' + (applies > 0 ? 'yes' : 'no') + ' sampled=' + (st.ticks >= 60 ? 'yes' : 'no'); return verdict === 'held' ? base : base + ' | ' + JSON.stringify({max: +st.max.toFixed(2), applies, ticks: st.ticks, bad: st.bad}); })()

assertions.desc: THE CONTROL for the first leg: the pointer sat on the News head before the click. NONE means the move coordinates missed - measure the layout frame and fix them, the verdicts mean nothing on a miss.

THE RULE on a folder: the glyph never rose above opacity 0 while the pointer held still across the fold's echoed rebuild. applies=no means no rebuild ran, so a 'held' would be vacuous; flashed@N is the bug, N is the worst frame.
THE CONTROL for the second leg: the pointer sat on the workspace name row.
THE RULE on the workspace row: same hold across the pinned fold's rebuild.
